faqs.a: Depends on distance and runner. A 5:30/km 10K is solid for a recreational runner; elites run under 3:00/km. Compare against your own history, not others.
faqs.q: What is a good running pace?

faqs.a: Divide 60 by the pace in minutes. 5:30/km = 5.5 min, so 60/5.5 = 10.9 km/h. This calculator does it live.
faqs.q: How do I convert min/km to km/h?

faqs.a: Treadmills measure belt speed; GPS measures position. Calibration, belt wear, and running form shift readings 2-5%. Trust one source per training block.
faqs.q: Why is my treadmill pace different from outdoor?

faqs.a: Roughly 15-25 seconds per km slower than your half-marathon pace, or 30-45 s/km slower than 10K pace. The time mode above turns any pace into a finish time.
faqs.q: What pace should I run a marathon at?

faqs.a: Run intervals at 5K-10K race pace (faster than easy pace by 30-60 s/km). Use the pace mode to convert a recent race into training paces.
Yes - about 80% of weekly running should be easy (1-2 min/km slower than 10K pace). Easy miles build the aerobic base that makes fast paces possible.

pace-calculator.formula:
Pace (sec/km) = total seconds / distance (km)
Speed (km/h) = 3600 / pace (sec/km) = 60 / pace (min/km)
Finish time = pace (sec/km) x distance (km)

Example: 10 km in 55:00
Pace = 3300 / 10 = 330 sec/km = 5:30/km
Speed = 3600 / 330 = 10.9 km/h
howTo: Choose 'Find pace' if you know distance and time, or 'Find time' for a target pace.
Enter the distance in kilometres and your time (or target pace).
Pace per km, per mile, and speed appear instantly.

Round training paces to the nearest 5-10 seconds - precision beyond that is noise.
keyFacts: Pace = time / distance (min/km). Speed = distance / time (km/h). They are reciprocals: km/h = 60 / pace-min-per-km.
1 mile = 1.60934 km. Multiply a per-km pace by 1.609 to get per-mile pace.
Race distances: 5K, 10K, half marathon 21.0975 km, marathon 42.195 km.
A 5:00/km pace = 12.0 km/h. A 4:00/km pace = 15.0 km/h.
GPS watches measure pace by distance; treadmills by belt speed - they often disagree by 2-5%.
Negative splits (second half faster) beat even pacing for most runners.

pace-calculator.quickAnswer: Pace is time divided by distance. Running 10 km in 55 minutes means 5:30 per km (55/10), which is 10.9 km/h. In miles that is 8:51 per mile. Flip it: at a 5:30/km pace, a marathon (42.2 km) takes about 3:52:04.
pace-calculator.tagline: Convert running pace, speed, and finish time - any two give you the third.
pace-calculator.workedExample:
You run 10 km in 55 minutes:
1. Total seconds: 55 x 60 = 3300.
2. Pace: 3300 / 10 = 330 sec/km = 5:30 per km.
3. Speed: 3600 / 330 = 10.9 km/h.
4. Per mile: 330 x 1.60934 = 531 sec = 8:51 per mile.

Target pace 5:30/km for a marathon (42.195 km):
1. 330 sec/km x 42.195 = 13924 sec.
2. 13924 / 3600 = 3.87 h = 3:52:04 finish.
